port.name: Posting
port.description: Living Code for Posting: native YAML palettes for HTTP requests, response status, syntax colors, focus and layered UI surfaces.

guide.installation:
```sh
git clone https://github.com/living-code-theme/posting.git
cd posting
```

Run `posting locate themes` to find your theme directory. On Linux with the default location:

```sh
mkdir -p "$HOME/.local/share/posting/themes"
cp themes/*.yaml "$HOME/.local/share/posting/themes/"
POSTING_THEME=living-code-night posting
```

Use the path reported by `posting locate themes` if it differs. Restart Posting after adding files.
guide.configuration: To keep a flavor permanently, set `theme: living-code-night` in Posting’s existing config. You can preview themes through **Ctrl+P → Theme…**. Each YAML file declares its name, light/dark appearance and all supported base palette colors. Posting derives HTTP method and syntax colors from those palette fields; no ignored legacy syntax blocks are shipped.
guide.compatibility: Targets Posting 3’s native palette API; the same base fields are also understood by Posting 2, but version-specific rendering is not claimed. Paper explicitly sets `dark: false`. `load_user_themes` must be enabled, and `theme_directory` may override the default location. Tests parse YAML and verify the documented supported field set.
